speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information considering the advances in artificial intelligence (AI) with platforms such as ChatGPT and the GPT-4 architecture, what attention is being given to promoting and ensuring (i) the development of ethical AI which responds in a manner consistent with human values and (ii) maintenance of ethical standards in the development, dataset training and deployment of AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Our approach was explained at the 19 April 2023 Sitting.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Deputy Speaker, I thank the Senior Minister of State for his answer.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The Senior Minister of State, in his example of the Public Service gaining experience with the use of ChatGPT and GPT-4, essentially alluded to the idea of a responsible person when AI is being deployed for a purpose.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I first ask the Senior Minister of State whether this approach will be encouraged in other settings, including in the private sector?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: So that, for example, if a firm uses AI to make decisions on human resources, there can be appropriate accountability if the AI results in discriminatory behaviour against job applicants.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: This is so that Singaporeans and members of the public interacting with an online portal can know whether the chat is being generated by an AI or by a fellow human being.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We hope through that platform, these best practices as well as the moves that the public sector is making can also influence the standards and approaches that occur in the private sector; and vice versa, as we learn best practices from the private sector for our role and mission in the public sector.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: On his second question about the role of a proof of human marker, I think it is something worth studying.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But I would caveat that it is not necessarily something that you may want to introduce as a general rule across all AI mechanisms.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think the Member would appreciate there are a fair number of tasks which can be very safely and reasonably automated without the need for demonstrating a human in the loop.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In our day-to-day work and our interactions with our many devices, we know that this is the type of technology that is being deployed safely and to good effect.
